clue.text: Finish first unpredictable race, expected last

parts.note: to finish something is to end it, so the word supplies END

indicators.note: placed before the three words that follow, it asks for the opening letter of each one

explanation.surface: A punter backs a horse to win an erratic race, though it was tipped to come in last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish first' looks like a racing result, but 'first' belongs to the next three words, whose initials give URE.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to hold out or survive over time, a plain synonym of the verb meaning to persist.

clue.text: Incident on cycle, losing helmet late in the day

indicators.note: the helmet sits on top, so the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A cyclist has an accident in the evening and loses a helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the period late in the day.

clue.text: Is nothing in part of Northern Ireland worthy of scorn?

indicators.note: says the first pieces sit inside the place name

parts.note: Derry is a city and county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A question whether a region of Northern Ireland that has nothing deserves contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means laughably small or ridiculous, deserving derision or scorn.

clue.text: Period before race to top of mountain

parts.note: going to the top of a mountain is going up

explanation.surface: The build-up to a hill race whose course climbs a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the preparatory period leading up to an event, such as the run-up to an election.

clue.text: Takes great delight in one's fast wheels

indicators.note: something that wheels turns round and round, so the letters of the words before it are spun into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters O, N, E, S

explanation.surface: A boy-racer is proud of a speedy set of wheels on a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' reads as a noun meaning a car, but it is a verb: the words before it are turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: To feast on something is an idiom for relishing or enjoying it greatly, as one would a banquet.

clue.text: Urging former lover of Emma H to suppress this, initially

indicators.note: the admiral's name holds down and encloses the letter that follows

parts.note: Horatio Nelson was the lover of Emma Hamilton; his first name plus his initial N

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word this

explanation.surface: Someone presses Emma Hamilton's old lover to keep something quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Horatio Nelson and Lady Emma Hamilton were famous lovers; HORATIO N encloses T.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhortation is an act of strongly encouraging or urging someone to do something.

clue.text: Spoil, say, good food

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to spoil or thwart it
EG, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a nice bit of cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a British snack: a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch egg is an item of food, so the general word covers it as an example.

clue.text: Scrawny local wearing blue

indicators.note: the blue is worn around the pub, enclosing it

parts.note: in Britain the local is the neighbourhood pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A thin regular at the pub is dressed in blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means very thin, a close synonym of scrawny.

clue.text: Small amount of egg wrapped up in loaf

indicators.note: says the turned word goes inside the head

parts.note: loaf is slang for head, as is nut

indicators.note: in a down entry, wrapped up means the word is turned to read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A little egg is wrapped up inside a loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf (as in 'use your loaf') and nut are both slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump or piece, so a small amount of something valuable.

clue.text: Rambling harangue beginning hesitantly

indicators.note: says the hesitation sound comes at the start of the tirade

parts.note: ER is the noise of someone speaking hesitantly

explanation.surface: A speaker starts a long, wandering tirade with nervous umming and erring.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering or roving, as in a knight errant, so it matches rambling in the sense of travelling aimlessly.

clue.text: Making film of gun crime

definitions.meaning: filming a movie or scene is called this on set
an incident in which someone is shot with a firearm

explanation.surface: A director makes a film about armed violence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both photographing a film and firing a gun at someone, two everyday senses.

clue.text: Ordeal for learners: steep part, with bends

indicators.note: bends twist the letters of the two words before them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A learner driver struggles on a stretch of road that is steep and winding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a driving test on a hilly road with bends; 'with bends' is the anagram signal on STEEP PART.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination sheet set for pupils is an ordeal for those still learning, a wry description of a school exam.

clue.text: Troublesome for British confronting climate change

parts.note: PRO means in favour of, for

indicators.note: the letters of climate are changed into another order

explanation.surface: Climate change is a difficult issue for Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Problematic means causing difficulty, a direct synonym of troublesome.

clue.text: Short story competition? No way

indicators.note: saying no to something removes it, so the street letters are taken away

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a common way

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a short-story contest is running, and is told it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' looks like a refusal, but 'No' signals removal of ST (way) from CONTEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A conte is a short tale, especially a French literary one, a word borrowed from French.

clue.text: Board members aim to speak formally

parts.note: to aim something is to direct it
to orate is to make a formal speech

explanation.surface: Members of a company board try to talk in an official manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of people who run an organisation, like the board of a company, is collectively a directorate.

clue.text: Craftsman who worries, getting shut inside?

indicators.note: the shut-in word goes inside the one who worries

parts.note: a carer is someone who cares, or worries

explanation.surface: A worried tradesman finds himself locked in.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a skilled woodworker, one example of a craftsman.

clue.text: At home, notice dog is kept safe? Hardly

indicators.note: the dog is held within the noticing word

explanation.surface: A householder sees a warning that the dog is safely shut away, but doubts it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means not safe or firmly fixed, so hardly safe.

clue.text: Learners boss sent for retraining

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud

indicators.note: retraining reshapes the letters of sent into a new order

explanation.surface: A manager is sent off for further training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a manager, but here it means a knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Students are people learning, so learners is a simple synonym.

clue.text: Rich bread bun, popular with gin and Vermouth

parts.note: a roll is a small bread bun
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in the drink gin and it

explanation.surface: A list of luxuries: fancy bread and a gin and vermouth cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: GIN AND IT is a British cocktail of gin with Italian vermouth, which is why vermouth gives IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling in it is an idiom for being very wealthy, as if wallowing in money.

clue.text: Verbally attacked boy hugging girl

indicators.note: the boy wraps around the girl

explanation.surface: A boy embraces a girl and gets told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out at someone in words is to criticise them fiercely, so lashed means attacked in speech.

clue.text: Drink brought in by sympathetic assistant

indicators.note: the letters are carried inside the two following words, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A kind helper brings someone a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Indian abandoning horse fast

indicators.note: the Indian leaves the horse behind, so its letter is dropped

parts.note: an Apache is a Native American
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A Native American rider leaves a horse and runs off quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means quickly or at speed, an adverb matching fast in that sense.

clue.text: Name of former pin-up in masculine environment

parts.note: MAN'S, belonging to a man, is masculine
a field is an area of activity or environment

explanation.surface: A glamour model worked in a world dominated by men.
explanation.walkthrough: Jayne Mansfield was an American actress and 1950s-60s pin-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Jayne Mansfield was a famous Hollywood sex symbol, so her surname is the name of a former pin-up.

clue.text: Clash with new playwright

parts.note: a fray is a fight or clash

explanation.surface: A dramatist argues with a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Frayn is an English dramatist, author of Noises Off and Copenhagen.

clue.text: Lack confidence to relax in the sun right away?

indicators.note: says the relaxing word goes inside the other piece
R, for right, is taken away

parts.note: the sun is the Earth's heater

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether to sunbathe straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but drops R; the sun is treated as the Earth's heater, and 'in' places the relaxing word inside, giving HEATE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause through uncertainty, which is lacking confidence to act.

clue.text: Old man's joke about a Pacific native

parts.note: PA is father, the old man

indicators.note: the joke goes around the letter A

explanation.surface: Dad tells a joke concerning someone from the Pacific islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A Papuan comes from Papua New Guinea, in the south-west Pacific, so is a Pacific native.

clue.text: Police inspector assigned to tough area

explanation.surface: A detective is posted to a rough neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is a region or locality, a straightforward synonym of area.

clue.text: English golfer/German philosopher

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: A puzzling pair of labels: an English sportsman alongside a German thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels was a German philosopher who co-wrote The Communist Manifesto with Marx.
